content:
Progress M-14M was an unmanned cargo spacecraft used by the Russian space agency Roscosmos to resupply the International Space Station (ISS). It was launched on August 24, 2012, aboard a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.

The spacecraft carried more than 2.5 tons of supplies, including food, water, fuel, and equipment, to the ISS. It successfully docked with the station on August 26, 2012, and remained attached for several months while the crew unloaded the cargo and filled it with waste material.

Progress M-14M undocked from the ISS on January 23, 2013, and re-entered Earth's atmosphere, burning up upon re-entry over the Pacific Ocean. The successful mission demonstrated Russia's ongoing ability to resupply the ISS and support the international space program.

Overall, Progress M-14M completed its mission successfully and contributed to the continued operation and support of the ISS.
